In the rear view, seen from behind, the back, haunches and tail are shown: the shoulders, torso, limbs and blade span are drawn at the same size as in the front view, and the tail curls in a compact S close beside the haunches with the hooked tip resting next to the hind leg, so the body fills the frame and sets the scale. request.prompt: A creature sprite for RimWorld: the wuum. Countless small bodies that all belong to one vast, spreading thing — every wuum is a cell of the same superorganism, working toward the same single purpose: grow, and keep growing. A wuum buds off a copy of itself every few days and needs almost nothing to eat. It bursts when it dies, and what bursts out burns like acid. It is a small, soft, blob-like body that looks like one cell of something larger, limbless and faceless, made of a lower main mass and one budding lobe rising from the top of it where it copies itself. The lower main mass is one consistent body volume: a rounded dome with a fixed height and a fixed transverse width. The front view (south) and the rear view (north) are opposite views of this same dome, with the same width, the same height, and matching left and right flanks that curve inward at the same rate; the north view shows the dome seen from behind, with the budding lobe at the same size and position as in the south view. The wider, lower profile appears only in the side views (east and west), where the body's length is shown. The budding lobe is a two-chamber structure about one third as wide as the body, with a fixed bulk and height relative to the lower mass; the two chambers overlap naturally and the lobe always reads as the same full, round, substantial form. Acid-bright fluid glows in chambers under a thin skin, held inside a firmly defined, more opaque membrane edge, so the contour is stronger than the interior glow. The membrane is matte and layered, with visible brush texture and painted shading, and highlights are small and localized to a few spots. Style: realistic, hand-painted vanilla RimWorld sprite with soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette, so the shape reads clearly at standard zoom.
